summary: Describes how Ethernet pseudowires, which carry Ethernet services across a packet network, can be used over MPLS transport networks. It builds on existing IETF procedures for Ethernet pseudowires over MPLS and discusses the requirements for the services provided. It is informational.

eli5.summary: Ethernet pseudowires are like tunnels that make two far-apart Ethernet networks feel like one wire. This explains how to run such tunnels over a network designed for carrier-style transport.

subtitle: Carrying Ethernet services across MPLS transport networks

tldr.problem: Carriers need to offer Ethernet service between distant locations, but the transport network is built on MPLS, a label-switching technology, which requires careful configuration to safely carry Ethernet traffic without losing reliability.
tldr.mechanism: This document shows how to provision an Ethernet pseudowire—a virtual Ethernet connection that encapsulates Ethernet frames and sends them through an MPLS network. The pseudowire rides inside MPLS label-switched paths (LSPs) configured to work without certain optimizations that would break the connection monitoring required for transport-grade service.
tldr.outcome: Operators can use existing, proven MPLS techniques to deliver Ethernet services reliably, meeting transport network requirements for management-only operation, IP-independent monitoring, and connection verification.

today: RFC 5994 is an Informational specification showing how to deliver Ethernet pseudowire services over MPLS transport networks. These techniques continue to be used by carriers to meet transport-grade service requirements, and the approach informed the design of MPLS-TP.

sections.title: Ethernet Over MPLS Transport
sections.content:
Carriers often need to offer Ethernet service—a direct Ethernet connection between two distant locations—but their network backbone uses MPLS, a packet-switching technology based on labels rather than IP addresses. An Ethernet pseudowire is a virtual Ethernet cable that traverses the MPLS network, allowing two Customer Equipment (CE) routers to exchange Ethernet frames as if they were connected by a direct wire.

This document describes a practical method: encapsulating raw Ethernet frames and sending them through an MPLS Packet Switched Network (PSN) configured to meet the requirements of MPLS-TP (MPLS Transport Profile)—a carrier-grade variant designed jointly by the IETF and ITU-T. The pseudowire rides on MPLS Label Switched Paths (LSPs) that carry traffic from one edge of the network to the other. Two Provider Edge (PE) routers at the network boundary maintain the pseudowire: PE1 at the client side and PE2 at the server side.
sections.eli5: A pseudowire is a pretend Ethernet cable that goes through an MPLS network. It lets distant Ethernet networks feel connected as if by a real cable.

sections.title: Pseudowire Setup and Configuration
sections.content:
The Ethernet pseudowire is configured by provisioning its encapsulation and labeling. The RFC specifies use of raw Ethernet encapsulation with a control word (a header that helps detect misconfigurations) and a sequence number set to zero. The pseudowire label itself is statically provisioned—manually configured on the provider equipment rather than negotiated automatically.

Unlike some MPLS mechanisms, the Pseudowire Setup and Maintenance Label Distribution Protocol (used to negotiate labels dynamically) is not required; the simplicity of static provisioning reduces complexity and aligns with the operator's requirement to manage the network with external configuration tools rather than dynamic protocols. All labels used in the server layer (the MPLS transport network) must be statically provisioned, and transport paths must be unidirectional or bidirectional point-to-point, not multipath.
sections.eli5: The pseudowire is set up by manually telling the network equipment which labels to use. This is simpler and more reliable than the network figuring it out on its own.

sections.title: Operations, Administration, and Monitoring
sections.content:
To ensure the pseudowire is working, the network must be able to detect failures and misconfigurations. The RFC specifies the use of VCCV (Virtual Circuit Connectivity Verification) with BFD (Bidirectional Forwarding Detection) for connection verification. BFD is a lightweight protocol that does not depend on IP routing, making it suitable for transport networks. Two profiles are defined: Profile 1 uses BFD without IP/UDP headers (suitable when PE routers are not IP-capable), and Profile 2 uses BFD with IP/UDP headers (suitable when they are IP-capable).

VCCV embeds the monitoring traffic inside the pseudowire itself, below the pseudowire label, so monitoring is not vulnerable to failures in the data path. This is critical: if monitoring took a different path through the network, a failure on the data path would not be detected by monitoring. Once VCCV is provisioned and the pseudowire is up, no other monitoring profile should be used until the pseudowire status changes to DOWN.
sections.eli5: The network regularly sends health checks through the pseudowire to make sure it is still working. The health checks travel the same path as the data, so if anything breaks, the health checks will fail too.

sections.title: MPLS Configuration and Constraints
sections.content:
The MPLS transport layer must be configured according to carrier-grade principles. Key constraints include: no PHP (Penultimate Hop Popping) on transport LSPs—the outer label must stay on until the packet reaches its final destination. No label merging is allowed on transport paths (unless it is deliberately enabled for fast re-route), ensuring a single end-to-end path rather than alternative routes. Equal Cost Multipath (ECMP) must not be configured, preventing load balancing that would split pseudowire traffic across multiple paths.

The network can use either E-LSP (EXP-Inferred-PSC LSP) or L-LSP (Label-Only-Inferred-PSC LSP) as defined in RFC 3270, supporting both packet-switched and circuit-oriented signaling. The EXP field supports only the pipe and short-pipe QoS models. These constraints ensure predictable, deterministic behavior suitable for transport networks where per-connection state and separation of control and data planes are required.
sections.eli5: The MPLS network is set up so that each pseudowire takes exactly one path with no tricks, and every packet follows that same route every time.
